_about: ONE SPANISH WORD FOR EACH ENGLISH TERM (the person, 25 October 2026: 'it's important to use consistent translations across different pages so that it's easier to follow and more uniform phrasing rather than describing it differently on each page'; the term list approved the same day).

Each term gives the English forms it is found by ('en') and the Spanish forms that render it ('es'); the first Spanish form is the rendering, the rest are the same words inflected or abbreviated. Every entry in es.json whose English uses the term must use one of the Spanish forms, and preflight names any that does not (i18n.term_faults). A form is matched as whole words, ignoring case unless it has a capital letter; markup and entities are read as the reader sees them.

'skip' lists English phrases that contain the term but are something else (State House is a building, not the House), and 'except' lists entries that use the English in another sense, each with the reason. An exception whose entry no longer exists is itself a fault, so the list cannot rot.

HOW A CHOICE IS MADE. A program's or an office's name follows the agency's own Spanish where it publishes one (Medicare, the Postal Service); where it publishes none, the English name stays with a Spanish gloss. Ordinary words (apply, eligible, fee, appointment) follow this list on every page, even where one agency phrases it differently. 'basis' says where each choice came from.
TO CHANGE A TERM, change it here first: preflight then names every entry to bring along, and src/ops/translations.py --set brings each one, back to draft for the proofreader.
